newsitem.title: USA: Md. unemployment rate rises to 4.5 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: Md. unemployment rate rises to 4.5 pct in May.

text.p: A seasonal increase in the number of job seekers nudged Maryland's unemployment rate to 4.5 percent in May from 4.4 percent in April, the state's Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation said Thursday.
On a seasonally-adjusted basis, the May rate dropped slightly, to 4.7 percent from 4.8 percent.
The number of residents holding jobs rose for the fourth consecutive month in May, to 2.6 million.

"Continued growth in the state's employment level is good news that reflects economic strength," Eugene Conti, the department's secretary, said in a statement. "The slight increase in the unemployment rate in May is not alarming. It reflects the seasonal trend that stems in part from high school and college students looking for summer jobs."
Local unemployment rates included lows of 2.3 percent in Montgomery County and 2.8 percent in Howard County, and highs of 12.1 percent in Garrett County and 9.4 percent in Somerset County.
